title: Count the mess without checking pairs
hook: How far is 2 4 1 3 5 from sorted? Must you compare every pair to find out?

knows: merging two sorted lists by taking the smaller front card (merge-sort-payoff)
doesNotKnow: that one pass of merging also counts how far a list is from sorted
that counting out-of-order pairs can cost far fewer than n(n-1)/2 checks

misconception: Counting out-of-order pairs means checking every pair, which is n(n-1)/2 checks.
objective: The learner can merge [2 4] and [1 3 5], add the number of left cards still waiting each time a right card is taken, reach 3 out-of-order pairs, and explain why this counting is free during merge sort (O(n log n) total).

claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): brute force over all 10 pairs gives exactly (2,1), (4,1), (4,3); control lists: 5 4 3 2 1 gives 10, 1 2 3 4 5 gives 0. Demo.tsx BRUTE recomputes the list for the reveal. Unverified.

claims.text: Each half, [2 4] and [1 3 5], is already in order, so no out-of-order pair sits inside a half.
When a right-half card is taken, it is smaller than every left card still waiting, so it forms one out-of-order pair with each: 1 jumps 2 and 4 (+2), 3 jumps 4 (+1), 5 jumps nobody.
claims.source: The left half is sorted and the merge takes the smaller front card, so a right card taken first is smaller than the left front and hence every waiting left card; each such left card came earlier in the list. Builder's node merge log: 1(+2), 2, 3(+1), 4, 5(+0). Demo.tsx STEPS recomputes it. Unverified.

claims.text: Counting during the merge gives the same answer as checking every pair.
claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): merge-sort count equals brute-force count on all 720 orders of 1..6 (brief cs.algorithms.md #54 claim 2). Unverified.

claims.text: Checking every pair of 5 cards takes 10 checks; the merge took 5 steps.
claims.source: 5 x 4 / 2 = 10 pairs; the merge takes one card per step, 5 cards. Unverified.

claims.text: Merge sort splits and merges at every level, so counting this way costs O(n log n) in total, not n².
claims.source: CLRS 4th ed. chapter 2, problem 2-4 (inversions: count in Theta(n lg n) worst case by modifying merge sort); 3rd ed. problem 2-4. Unverified.

recall.question: During a merge, a card from the right half is taken while 3 cards still wait in the left half. How many out-of-order pairs does that one step reveal?
recall.why: The taken card is smaller than every left card still waiting, and each of them came earlier, so it makes one out-of-order pair with each of the 3.
